issues.body: `iriref_end` treats any `<` followed by only IRIREF-permitted bytes up to a later `>` as an IRI, but that condition is not sufficient to distinguish an IRIREF from operators. For example, in compact tokenization such as `FILTER(?a<1&&FLTR(?o)&&?b>2)`, the bytes from `<` through `>` contain none of the excluded IRIREF characters, so the scanner skips the entire span and fails to report `FLTR`. SPARQL punctuation/operators delimit these tokens without requiring whitespace. This is the same correctness class as round 1, and the new tests only cover spaced comparisons that return `None` at the first space.
issues.fix_hint: Use actual lexical context (or the SPARQL lexer) to decide whether `<` starts IRIREF rather than validating only the candidate body. Add an integration regression using compact comparisons on both sides of `FLTR`, such as `FILTER(?a<1&&FLTR(?o)&&?b>2)`, and assert the `FILTER` suggestion is present while genuine IRIREFs remain ignored.
issues.title: Compact comparison expressions are still swallowed as IRIREFs

verdict.summary: The round-1 defect is narrowed but not eliminated. `iriref_end` now recognizes spaced `<` comparisons, yet it still identifies `<...>` solely from the characters through the next `>`, without lexical context. Compact SPARQL expressions can therefore be mistaken for IRIREFs and hide a misspelled keyword. The added integration test exercises only comparisons containing spaces, so it does not cover this remaining acceptance-set mismatch.
